gaps.concept: Overt primary thyrotoxicosis produces suppressed TSH with elevated free T4 and/or T3.
gaps.why_tested: Enables interpretation of thyroid function tests before identifying the cause.

gaps.concept: Subclinical hyperthyroidism has suppressed TSH with normal free T4 and T3; T3 toxicosis has elevated T3 despite normal free T4.
gaps.why_tested: Enables diagnosis when a low TSH is paired with a normal free T4.

gaps.concept: Graves disease causes diffusely increased radioactive iodine uptake; destructive thyroiditis causes low uptake because hormone is released from damaged follicles.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes increased hormone synthesis from release of stored hormone on an uptake scan.

gaps.concept: Graves histology shows diffuse follicular hyperplasia, tall crowded epithelium, and scalloped colloid from active resorption.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies Graves disease from a thyroid biopsy image.

gaps.concept: A vascular thyroid bruit favors Graves disease and reflects increased gland blood flow.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes a diffuse Graves goiter from other causes of thyrotoxicosis on examination.

gaps.concept: Graves orbitopathy enlarges extraocular muscle bellies while sparing their tendons on orbital imaging.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies thyroid eye disease on CT or MRI.

gaps.concept: Graves orbitopathy can persist or occur without biochemical hyperthyroidism because it is an autoimmune manifestation.
gaps.why_tested: Explains eye findings in a patient whose thyroid hormone levels are normal.

gaps.concept: Painless and postpartum thyroiditis often have anti-TPO antibodies; postpartum immune rebound can produce a hyperthyroid phase followed by hypothyroidism.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes transient postpartum thyroiditis from postpartum Graves disease.

gaps.concept: Thionamides do not treat the thyrotoxic phase of destructive thyroiditis because new thyroid hormone synthesis is not increased.
gaps.why_tested: Tests treatment choice in a patient with thyrotoxicosis and low radioactive iodine uptake.

gaps.concept: Painful subacute thyroiditis is treated with anti-inflammatory therapy; its elevated ESR helps distinguish it from painless thyroiditis.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes two low-uptake thyroiditides in a patient with neck pain.

gaps.concept: Hashimoto thyroiditis can initially cause transient thyrotoxicosis, called hashitoxicosis, through follicular destruction.
gaps.why_tested: Explains elevated thyroid hormones in a patient with anti-TPO antibodies and low uptake.

gaps.concept: An iodine load can trigger Jod-Basedow hyperthyroidism in an autonomous thyroid nodule or multinodular goiter.
gaps.why_tested: Explains thyrotoxicosis after iodinated contrast in a patient with nodular thyroid disease.

gaps.concept: Amiodarone type 1 thyrotoxicosis reflects iodine-driven synthesis; type 2 reflects destructive thyroiditis.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes two mechanisms of thyrotoxicosis in a patient taking amiodarone.

gaps.concept: PTU and methimazole inhibit thyroid peroxidase, blocking iodide organification and coupling of iodotyrosines.
gaps.why_tested: Tests the molecular target of either antithyroid drug.

gaps.concept: High-dose iodide acutely inhibits thyroid hormone release and organification; in thyroid storm it follows a thionamide to avoid fueling synthesis.
gaps.why_tested: Explains the order of medications used in thyroid storm.

gaps.concept: Propranolol reduces adrenergic symptoms and, at high doses, inhibits peripheral conversion of T4 to T3.
gaps.why_tested: Tests why propranolol has effects beyond heart-rate control in severe thyrotoxicosis.

gaps.concept: PTU can cause ANCA-associated small-vessel vasculitis.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies a drug adverse effect in a patient receiving PTU for Graves disease.

gaps.concept: Radioactive iodine ablation commonly causes permanent hypothyroidism.
gaps.why_tested: Tests the expected long-term consequence of definitive Graves treatment.

gaps.concept: Thyrotoxic periodic paralysis causes episodic weakness and hypokalemia from beta-adrenergic stimulation of skeletal-muscle Na⁺/K⁺-ATPase.
gaps.why_tested: Explains sudden weakness and low potassium in a patient with thyrotoxicosis.

gaps.concept: Older adults may have apathetic thyrotoxicosis: weight loss or atrial fibrillation without prominent tremor or hyperactivity.
gaps.why_tested: Recognizes hyperthyroidism despite absent classic adrenergic symptoms.

gaps.concept: Maternal TSH-receptor stimulating antibodies cross the placenta and can cause transient neonatal Graves disease.
gaps.why_tested: Explains neonatal thyrotoxicosis in an infant born to a mother with Graves disease.

gaps.concept: A TSH-secreting pituitary adenoma causes high T4/T3 with an inappropriately normal or elevated TSH.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes central hyperthyroidism from typical primary thyrotoxicosis using laboratory results.

gaps.concept: Thyroid hormone resistance, often due to THRB mutation, can also produce high T4/T3 with nonsuppressed TSH.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes inherited hormone resistance from a TSH-secreting pituitary tumor.

gaps.concept: Riedel thyroiditis causes a hard, fixed fibrotic goiter and is associated with IgG4-related disease.
gaps.why_tested: Distinguishes fibrosing thyroiditis from malignancy in a patient with a woody thyroid mass.

gaps.concept: Graves thyroid acropachy causes finger clubbing and periosteal bone formation, usually alongside orbitopathy or pretibial myxedema.
gaps.why_tested: Identifies an uncommon extrathyroidal Graves manifestation from hand findings.
